# Travel insurance comparison

Annual multi-trip for the four of us, Europe only, renewing 15 Sept 2024. Trips in the next 12 months: Málaga half term (Oct 2024, me and Isla only), Galicia in August 2025 to see Javier's parents, maybe Paris at Easter.

## Must-haves

- Medical: at least £5m. Anything lower is a red flag even in Europe
- Cancellation: £3,000 per person, Galicia flights plus Paris Eurostar would be about £1,800 total
- Pre-existing conditions declared and **covered**: Theo's asthma (two inhalers, no hospital admission in 2 years), my thyroid (levothyroxine 75 mcg)
- Children covered when travelling with either parent, not only both
- Excess £100 or less per claim, ideally per person not per section
- Trip length limit at least 31 days (August trip is 18)

## Why not the free card cover

The Amex Gold travel cover came with the card I had open for the points (see [[Credit card churning]]). Read the wording: pre-existing conditions are excluded entirely, and it only applies if trips are paid for on the card. Theo's asthma is the obvious thing that would go wrong abroad. Also the card is closed now.

## Why not the bank account

FlexPlus was tempting at "free" but it isn't: £18 a month is £216 a year, and the only other perk I use is the mobile phone cover. If I ever drop the account I lose the travel cover mid-year. Plus £42 for the asthma screening.

## Picked: Aviva Family annual

- £84.00, policy AV-TRV-88213, 15 Sept 2024 to 14 Sept 2025
- Both conditions declared on the phone, screening ref MED-SCR-40291. Took 11 minutes
- Covers Isla travelling with only me (checked clause 4.2, yes)
- 31-day maximum trip, 31 days of total trips? NO, it's per trip, unlimited trips. Checked twice

## GHIC

Got GHIC cards for all four (free, gov.uk, NOT the paid sites that charge £20). Isla's arrived 2 Oct 2024. Card number ends 0912. GHIC covers state treatment in the EU but not repatriation, not private clinics, not cancellation. It is not a substitute.

## The one claim

Málaga, 25 Oct 2024: Isla's suitcase came off the carousel with the shell cracked. Iberia gave a PIR (AGP-IB-24117). Aviva paid £62 for the case after £100 excess? No: I tried, it was under the excess. Iberia paid €45 directly in December. Lesson: for small things go to the airline first. Packing light helps too: [[Packing list carry-on]].

## Long haul, later

If Vietnam happens in 2026 (Javier's idea), annual Europe won't cover it. Worldwide excluding USA from Aviva was £141. Visa side: [[Visa for Vietnam]]. Medical cost differences between countries come up in [[Health insurance deductible]].
